title: Karnaugh Map Solver
description: Minimize 2 to 4 variable Boolean functions with a real Quine–McCluskey solver: see the K-map grid, essential prime implicant groupings, and the minimized sum-of-products expression.
howto: Choose 2, 3 or 4 variables and type the minterm numbers (comma separated) in the Σm box.
Optionally type don't-care numbers in the Σd box (must not overlap with minterms).
Press Solve to get the minimized expression, the K-map grid with colored groupings, and the prime implicant steps.
Copy the minimized sum-of-products expression with the Copy button.

faqs.q: How does the solver find the minimized expression?
faqs.a: It runs the Quine–McCluskey algorithm: all minterms and don't-cares are repeatedly combined into larger implicants until only prime implicants remain, then essential prime implicants are selected via a prime implicant chart and any leftover minterms are covered greedily.
Input combinations whose output does not matter. The solver may treat them as 0 or 1, whichever gives a smaller expression — they can only help reduce the number of terms, never hurt.

faqs.q: Why is the K-map column order 00, 01, 11, 10?
faqs.a: That is Gray code order: only one bit changes between adjacent cells, which is what makes visual grouping valid. Group sizes must be powers of two (1, 2, 4, 8).
